record.paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures on Rational Systems in Three Dimensions
record.original_question: Consider the three-dimensional rational system, for n = 0, 1, ..., with nonnegative parameters and nonnegative initial conditions such that all denominators are positive: x_{n+1} = (alpha_1 + beta_1 x_n + gamma_1 y_n + delta_1 z_n)/(A_1 + B_1 x_n + C_1 y_n + D_1 z_n), y_{n+1} = (alpha_2 + beta_2 x_n + gamma_2 y_n + delta_2 z_n)/(A_2 + B_2 x_n + C_2 y_n + D_2 z_n), and z_{n+1} = (alpha_3 + beta_3 x_n + gamma_3 y_n + delta_3 z_n)/(A_3 + B_3 x_n + C_3 y_n + D_3 z_n). Across the 11,390,625 special cases of this system, what is the boundedness characterization of each special case, and are there general boundedness patterns analogous to those found in two-dimensional rational systems?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the three-dimensional rational system of difference equations
  x_{n+1} = (α₁ + β₁ xₙ + γ₁ yₙ + δ₁ zₙ)/(A₁ + B₁ xₙ + C₁ yₙ + D₁ zₙ),
  y_{n+1} = (α₂ + β₂ xₙ + γ₂ yₙ + δ₂ zₙ)/(A₂ + B₂ xₙ + C₂ yₙ + D₂ zₙ),
  z_{n+1} = (α₃ + β₃ xₙ + γ₃ yₙ + δ₃ zₙ)/(A₃ + B₃ xₙ + C₃ yₙ + D₃ zₙ),
for n = 0, 1, 2, …, where all 24 parameters α_i, β_i, γ_i, δ_i, A_i, B_i, C_i, D_i (i = 1, 2, 3) are nonnegative real numbers and the initial conditions (x₀, y₀, z₀) are nonnegative reals chosen so that every denominator is positive for all n ≥ 0. A "special case" is obtained by setting some subset of the parameters in each numerator and denominator to zero (so that the numerator and denominator of each component are nonzero linear combinations), yielding a total of 11,390,625 distinct such special cases.

A solution {(xₙ, yₙ, zₙ)} is called bounded if there exists M < ∞ such that xₙ, yₙ, zₙ ≤ M for all n ≥ 0, and the special case is said to have the boundedness property when every admissible solution is bounded.

Problem: For each of the 11,390,625 special cases, determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the (nonzero) parameters and the admissible initial conditions under which every solution is bounded. Moreover, identify general structural patterns characterizing boundedness across these special cases that are analogous to the boundedness classification known for the two-dimensional rational systems
  x_{n+1} = (α₁ + β₁ xₙ + γ₁ yₙ)/(A₁ + B₁ xₙ + C₁ yₙ),
  y_{n+1} = (α₂ + β₂ xₙ + γ₂ yₙ)/(A₂ + B₂ xₙ + C₂ yₙ).
artifact.status_search_result: Search results indicate ongoing work on boundedness of particular three-dimensional rational difference systems, with various authors treating isolated special cases (e.g., Alayachi 2021; Camouzis–Ladas work on rational systems). No complete classification of boundedness across all 11,390,625 special cases of the general three-dimensional first-order linear-fractional system has been found, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On the Solutions of Three-Dimensional Rational Difference Equation Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Studies boundedness and solution form for particular three-dimensional rational systems.
status_evidence.claim: Only isolated special cases are treated; no full classification given.

status_evidence.title: Boundedness of Solutions of a Rational System
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates boundedness for a specific rational system, indicating that boundedness analysis remains a piecewise effort.
status_evidence.claim: Boundedness analysis of rational systems is treated case by case.
